## DAILY INTELLIGENCE BRIEF

### 1. CIA director held intelligence talks in Moscow
CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow for contacts with Russian intelligence officials but did not meet President Vladimir Putin. President Donald Trump characterized the visit as “semi-routine.” Ukraine, which was reportedly asked to avoid striking Moscow and St. Petersburg during the trip, is still awaiting a promised U.S. briefing.

**Why it matters:** Direct U.S.-Russian intelligence engagement could provide a channel for managing escalation. Kyiv’s exclusion from the immediate readout may also raise questions about coordination during the war.

### 2. Russia escalated rhetoric and military signaling toward Japan
State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin invoked Russia’s nuclear status while rejecting Japan’s claims to the southern Kuril Islands. The warning followed Vladimir Putin’s first visit to disputed Iturup/Etorofu and Russian missile drills nearby involving a nuclear submarine, missile cruiser and coastal missile system.

**Why it matters:** The combination of nuclear rhetoric, a high-profile territorial visit and military exercises increases tensions in Northeast Asia, where the unresolved dispute has prevented a formal Russia-Japan peace treaty.

### 3. Russian occupation authorities imposed a 14-year treason sentence over a small Ukrainian military donation
A court in occupied Berdiansk sentenced a 74-year-old woman to 14 years in prison for transferring approximately $34 to Ukraine’s armed forces. The article also cited a separate case involving a Ukrainian detained in occupied Crimea over a $27 defense-related contribution.

**Why it matters:** The cases indicate severe punishment for low-level financial support to Ukraine and illustrate the use of Russian treason laws to enforce control in occupied territories.

### 4. Sikorsky established its first authorized EU Black Hawk parts hub
Czech company ČLS will operate the first authorized Black Hawk parts distribution center within the European Union, supporting more than 150 helicopters and several variants currently operating across the bloc.

**Why it matters:** Locating spare parts inside the EU should shorten supply chains and improve readiness for European military, security and emergency-response fleets.

## WATCH

- **Outcome of the CIA’s Moscow contacts:** Whether Washington briefs Kyiv and whether the talks produce further intelligence or deconfliction arrangements.
- **Russia-Japan tensions:** Additional Russian deployments, exercises or Japanese diplomatic and security responses around the disputed islands.
- **Jerusalem:** Israeli authorities reportedly detained the Palestinian minister for Jerusalem affairs near Al-Aqsa; the circumstances and potential effect on tensions at the site require clarification.

### 1. Major Cross-Border Disaster at China–Nepal Frontier
A landslide and debris-laden flood struck the Gyirong border area, causing heavy casualties on both sides. China reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet, while Nepalese police reported at least 97 deaths and 54 rescues. Nepal’s Tourism Board separately listed 384 people as missing; authorities were still verifying totals.

**Why it matters:** The scale of the missing-person reports indicates a major humanitarian emergency requiring sustained rescue operations and likely coordination between China and Nepal.

### 2. Strategic Gyirong Border Crossing Disrupted
The disaster damaged roads and disrupted communications and electricity around Gyirong Port. China closed vehicle routes between Gyirong town and the crossing except for emergency traffic.

**Why it matters:** Gyirong is a major land route for bilateral trade and cross-border movement. A prolonged closure could impede commerce, passenger travel and delivery of emergency assistance.

### 3. Landslide May Have Triggered Cascading Flood
A preliminary satellite-based assessment indicated that a snow-and-rock landslide near the border sent debris into the Lhende River, producing a destructive flood along the Lhende and Bhotekoshi river systems. Authorities continued to assess the cause and full impact.

**Why it matters:** The event highlights the exposure of Himalayan border infrastructure and communities to cascading landslide and flood hazards, including risks extending across national boundaries.

### WATCH
- Reconciliation of conflicting casualty and missing-person figures as rescue operations continue.
- The duration of the Gyirong Port closure and its effects on China–Nepal trade and transport.

President Donald Trump described the visit as “semi-routine,” while the Kremlin called the contacts positive and said Ratcliffe did not meet President Vladimir Putin. Ukraine reportedly has not yet received a promised U.S. briefing and was asked to avoid strikes on Moscow and St. Petersburg during the visit.

**Why it matters:** The visit indicates continued high-level security communication between Washington and Moscow despite the war in Ukraine. Kyiv’s reported exclusion from immediate briefings may raise concerns about transparency and coordination with Ukraine.

**What happened:** State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin invoked Russia’s nuclear status while rejecting Japan’s claims to the Russian-controlled southern Kuril Islands. His comments followed Putin’s visit to disputed Iturup/Etorofu and Russian missile drills in the area involving naval and coastal systems.

**Why it matters:** The rhetoric and military activity deepen tensions with Japan, which has sanctioned Russia over the Ukraine war. The territorial dispute continues to prevent a formal postwar peace treaty and could intensify security competition in Northeast Asia.

### Occupation Court Imposes 14-Year Treason Sentence

**What happened:** A court in Russian-occupied Berdiansk sentenced a 74-year-old woman to 14 years in prison for transferring approximately $34 to Ukraine’s armed forces. Russian authorities classified the payment as high treason. Other Ukrainians have reportedly faced similar prosecutions over small contributions to Ukrainian defense initiatives.

**Why it matters:** The case demonstrates the use of Russian treason law to punish financial support for Ukraine in occupied territory. Such prosecutions reinforce coercive control over residents and highlight continuing legal and human-rights concerns under Russian occupation.

### Israeli authorities detain Palestinian Jerusalem affairs minister

Middle East Monitor reported that Israeli authorities detained the Palestinian minister for Jerusalem affairs near the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound. No details on the circumstances, duration or stated grounds for the detention were provided.

**Why it matters:** Al-Aqsa and Jerusalem are highly sensitive political and religious flashpoints. The detention of a senior Palestinian official near the site could increase Israeli-Palestinian friction and prompt diplomatic or public reactions.

### Iranian athlete reports UAE entry ban and visa cancellation

Iranian bodybuilder Hadi Choopan said the United Arab Emirates denied him entry and canceled his 10-year UAE visa while he was attempting to travel through Dubai to pursue a US visa. He cited political conditions and travel restrictions in withdrawing from the 2026 Mr. Olympia competition.

**Why it matters:** The case illustrates how regional entry controls and US visa barriers can affect Iranian travelers. The article does not establish whether the UAE action reflects a wider policy change.

### Qatar and Saudi Arabia retain prominent regional sports roles

Iran’s football federation said the national team will probably hold a 12-day training camp in Doha before the 2027 Asian Cup, which Saudi Arabia will host from January 7 to February 5.

**Why it matters:** Although primarily a sporting development, it highlights Qatar’s continuing role as a regional training and events hub and Saudi Arabia’s expanding use of major international sports competitions to strengthen its regional and global profile.

### WATCH

- Whether Israeli authorities release further information about the Palestinian minister’s detention and whether it triggers protests or official diplomatic responses.
- Whether additional Iranians report UAE visa cancellations or entry denials, which could indicate broader travel restrictions.

articles.title: Russian-Occupied Berdiansk Court Jails 74-Year-Old Woman for 14 Years Over $34 Ukraine Army Donation
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Russian-Occupied Berdiansk Court Jails 74-Year-Old Woman for 14 Years Over $34 Ukraine Army Donation
A court in Russian-occupied Berdiansk has sentenced a 74-year-old woman to 14 years in prison for financially supporting the Armed Forces of Ukraine after she transferred UAH 1,500 (approximately $34) to the Ukrainian military.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Radio Liberty/Radio Free Europe on August 26, the woman, born in 1952, was convicted of high treason over the donation, which investigators said was made through a Ukrainian banking application in 2024.
Russian authorities alleged that following the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the woman developed what they described as a “persistent negative attitude toward representatives of Russian state authorities.”
Investigators said she subsequently transferred UAH 1,500 to support the Ukrainian Armed Forces. Russian law enforcement authorities claimed that the payment harmed Russia’s security and formed the basis for the treason charge.
On February 27, 2022, Russian forces entered Berdiansk, a port city on the Sea of Azov in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, as they advanced through southern Ukraine during the opening days of the full-scale invasion.
Russian troops subsequently seized the city’s administrative buildings and established control over Berdiansk. Local authorities refused to cooperate with the occupying forces, while the city’s police department was disbanded and public transportation was suspended.
In another case, Russian FSB officers detained 34-year-old Ukrainian Liudmyla Kolesnikova while she was attending her mother’s funeral in temporarily occupied Yalta, Crimea, later accusing her of treason over a $27 contribution to Ukrainian defense efforts.
Kolesnikova, who had lived in Ireland since 2022, was held incommunicado for three months. She was accused of “treason through espionage” for purchasing two “Russian warship” NFT stamps sold to raise funds for Ukrainian drone production. The FSB reportedly discovered the transaction after accessing her phone. If convicted, she could face up to 20 years in prison.
In 2025, Russian courts have also handed down lengthy sentences in other treason cases. Nuclear engineer Ruslan Shadiyev was sentenced to 18 years in a maximum-security penal colony after being convicted of “state treason” and “assisting terrorist activity,”

articles.title: Trump says CIA chief's Russia trip was 'semi-routine' as Ukraine still awaits briefing
articles.body:
Trump says CIA chief's Russia trip was 'semi-routine' as Ukraine still awaits briefing
CIA Director John Ratcliffe's trip to Moscow was "semi-routine," U.S. President Donald Trump said on Aug. 26, rejecting speculation that the visit was intended to warn Russia against possible action targeting NATO countries.
The comments came as Ukraine has yet to receive information about the contents or outcome of Ratcliffe's meetings in Moscow, according to a source familiar with the matter. The U.S. side had earlier promised to brief Ukrainian officials after the trip.
"He's there on very sort of semi-routine (business) — I hate to disappoint people," Trump said.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Aug. 26 that Ratcliffe did not meet directly with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The Russian president was instead briefed on the details of the meetings, Peskov said.
"There were contacts with the intelligence services," Peskov told reporters, describing the talks as a "positive development" between U.S. and Russian intelligence agencies.
The visit was first reported after a U.S. military C-17A Globemaster III aircraft was spotted at a Moscow airport, prompting speculation about the purpose of Ratcliffe's trip.
Ukraine was asked to refrain from striking Moscow and St. Petersburg while Ratcliffe was in Russia, according to a source familiar with the matter.
"They don't believe in the strength of Putin's air defenses," the source said.

articles.title: Russia Waves Nuclear Threat at Japan as Kuril Islands Dispute Escalates
articles.body:

Russia Waves Nuclear Threat at Japan as Kuril Islands Dispute Escalates
Vyacheslav Volodin, speaker of Russia’s State Duma, invoked Moscow’s nuclear arsenal while warning Japan over its territorial claims to the disputed Kuril Islands, marking another escalation in already worsening tensions between the two countries.
Volodin accused Tokyo on August 26 of adopting increasingly confrontational rhetoric over the islands and repeated Moscow’s claim that the disputed territory is an “integral part” of Russia.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Volodin then pointed directly to Russia’s status as a nuclear-armed state while attacking Japan’s position.
“Let them remember the times when militarist Japan killed millions of civilians. Now they are trying to return to the same rhetoric. They should not. A nuclear power such as Russia cannot be defeated,” Volodin said.
The remarks come less than two weeks after Russian leader Vladimir Putin traveled to Iturup, known in Japan as Etorofu, on August 13 in a visit that triggered a sharp protest from Tokyo.
It was Putin’s first visit to the disputed island chain during his time in power.
Japan claims four southern islands controlled by Russia—Etorofu, known in Russia as Iturup; Kunashiri, known as Kunashir; Shikotan; and the Habomai islets. Tokyo collectively refers to them as the Northern Territories.
The Soviet Union seized the islands at the end of World War II, and the decades-long territorial dispute has prevented Japan and Russia from signing a formal postwar peace treaty.
Following Putin’s visit, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reaffirmed Tokyo’s territorial claim and described the Russian leader’s trip to Etorofu as “absolutely unacceptable.”
Japan also lodged a formal protest with Moscow.
Russia, meanwhile, has rejected Tokyo’s claims and increasingly framed Japan’s position as evidence of renewed militarism, particularly as relations between the two countries have deteriorated since Japan joined Western sanctions against Moscow over Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine.
In addition, days after Putin’s first-ever visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, Russia staged rare missile drills nearby—using a nuclear submarine, a missile cruiser, and a Bastion coastal system in a fresh show of force toward Japan.

articles.title: Researchers quantify the rate of “mercy sex” among women with low sexual desire
articles.body:
Women experiencing a chronic lack of sexual desire still routinely engage in sexual activity with their partners, a behavior researchers have quantified as happening about two and a half times per month. These baseline events, often motivated by relationship obligations rather than personal arousal, could alter how medical treatments for low sexual desire are evaluated. The findings were published in the Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy.
Hypoactive sexual desire disorder is a condition where a person persistently lacks sexual thoughts or desire, leading to personal distress. Clinical trials for treatments often measure success by tracking an increase in sexually satisfying events. A sexually satisfying event is defined as any sexual activity, from intercourse to manual stimulation, that a participant considers fulfilling.
In 2015, the Food and Drug Administration approved the first drug for premenopausal women with this condition. During the evaluation process, the agency required pharmaceutical companies to measure success using criteria similar to those used for male erectile dysfunction. This meant focusing heavily on the frequency of sexual events. The disorder is fundamentally a cognitive dysfunction related to a lack of mental desire, whereas erectile dysfunction is often tied to vascular or anatomical issues. Using event frequency to measure a psychological lack of desire created a mismatch in the data.
Nikita Guptan and James A. Simon, researchers at IntimMedicine Specialists in Washington, D.C., noticed a pattern in these trials. Women diagnosed with a complete lack of sexual desire were still logging multiple sexual events before receiving any medication. Guptan and Simon sought to quantify this baseline activity, which they termed mercy sex.
The researchers define this behavior as consensual participation in sexual acts not for personal arousal, but to fulfill a perceived obligation. By examining these baseline numbers, the authors aimed to understand the prevalence of this behavior and explore the social and psychological reasons behind it.
The researchers analyzed baseline data from multiple randomized, placebo-controlled trials spanning nearly a decade. These trials tested three different medical treatments for low sexual desire. The researchers first looked at four clinical trials evaluating a testosterone patch, which included a large sample of 2,204 naturally and surgically menopausal women.
In these testosterone studies, the baseline frequency of sexual events remained highly consistent. Across the different trial groups, the women reported an average of 2.5 to 2.9 sexually satisfying events per 28 days. This rate showed very little variation regardless of whether the women were naturally menopausal, surgically menopausal, or taking hormone therapies.
Next, Guptan and Simon evaluated data from clinical trials testing flibanserin, an oral medication approved for low sexual desire. They reviewed four trials conducted in the United States, comprising a large sample of 3,413 women. The baseline data for these trials showed a similar pattern, with women reporting between 2.0 and 3.0 sexually satisfying events every 28 days.
The researchers noted that older participants tended to report slightly lower frequencies. A trial focusing on naturally menopausal women with an average age of 55 reported the lowest baseline frequency at 2.0 events. Trials focusing on younger, premenopausal women with an average age of 36 reported frequencies closer to 3.0 events per month.
The researchers also examined an unpublished flibanserin trial conducted across 13 European countries, which included 915 participants. The European data averaged 2.41 baseline events per month, closely mirroring the United States findings. The rates varied widely between individual countries, ranging from 4.19 events per month in the Czech Republic to 1.12 in Italy.
Finally, the authors analyzed two trials evaluating bremelanotide, an injectable medication for low sexual desire. These two trials included over 1,200 women. The baseline frequencies in these studies were notably lower, averaging about 1.2 events per month. The researchers attribute this lower number to the specific design of the bremelanotide trials, which included a four-week observation period where participants took a placebo before the actual baseline measurements were finalized.
Guptan and Simon suggest a biopsychosocial framework to explain why women with low desire consistently engage in sexual activity. From an evolutionary perspective, women may participate in sex to maintain stability and prevent their partners from seeking intimacy elsewhere.
According to sexual selection research, males and females often have different reproductive strategies. Short-term mating strategies might benefit males seeking multiple partners, but they can disadvantage females who historically required stability and resource sharing to raise offspring.
The authors hypothesize that women may have learned to keep their male partners monogamous by fulfilling their faster-paced reproductive desires. In modern contexts, this translates to engaging in obligatory sex as a defense mechanism to preserve a long-term relationship. One qualitative study cited by the authors featured a patient who reported forcing herself to have sex to prevent her husband from satisfying his needs with someone else.
The authors suggest that women might also use sex as a tool to fulfill a psychological need for emotional closeness, even if the physical desire is absent. The authors reference Rosemary Basson’s circular model of sexual response, a psychological framework suggesting that female sexual arousal is highly nuanced and often driven by a need for emotional connection rather than spontaneous physical hunger.
Because men are socially conditioned to associate physical sex with emotional closeness, women may engage in sex simply to maintain that emotional bond. They learn to accept the physical act as a replacement for pure emotional intimacy, complying with their partner’s expectations to avoid conflict or emotional distance.
Social and religious conditioning can play a role in setting expectations for marital duties as well. The authors noted that countries with historically strict religious frameworks regarding marital obligations, such as Catholic teachings on conjugal debt, often showed varying rates of this behavior. Italy, for instance, had the lowest reported rate, which the authors speculate might relate to cultural shifts following the 1968 decriminalization of female adultery.
The analyzed data relies on samples limited to heterosexual women in monogamous relationships. The proposed explanations regarding partner dynamics and evolutionary pressures do not reflect the experiences of women in non-heterosexual relationships or those without regular partners.
The use of the term “satisfying” in these clinical trials is highly subjective. A participant might log an event as satisfying because it fostered emotional intimacy or resolved a relationship conflict, rather than providing physical gratification.
Future researchers designing clinical trials for sexual dysfunction will need to differentiate between an increase in actual sexual desire and an increase in obligatory sexual events. If clinical success is measured purely by the frequency of sexual activity, a drug’s true effect on internal desire could be misjudged.
The study, “Quantification of “Mercy Sex” in Heterosexual Women,” was authored by Nikita Guptan and James A. Simon.

articles.title: Sikorsky opens first EU Black Hawk parts hub
articles.body:
Sikorsky has selected Czech aviation company ČLS as its first authorised Black Hawk parts distribution centre in the European Union, supporting more than 150 helicopters already in service across the bloc.
Sikorsky has appointed Česká letecká servisní, known as ČLS, as its first authorised distribution centre for Black Hawk helicopter parts in the European Union, according to the company.
The agreement is intended to improve access to replacement components for the more than 150 Black Hawk helicopters currently operating across EU countries. ČLS will be able to stock Sikorsky-recommended parts at its warehouse, allowing frequently required components to be held closer to European operators rather than sourced through longer international supply chains.
The new arrangement will support several variants of the Black Hawk family, including the S-70, UH-60M and UH-60A/L. According to Lockheed Martin, the growing number of aircraft in European service has increased the importance of faster access to spares and sustainment support.
Rich Benton, vice president and general manager of Sikorsky, said, as quoted in a news update: “As the Hawk helicopter fleet grows in Europe, we are committed to supporting operator readiness for emergency response, security operations and more.”
He added: “By working alongside ČLS, we are strengthening our service footprint in the European Union and ensuring timely parts delivery for Black Hawk helicopters.”
ČLS has experience providing avionics, special mission equipment, modernisation and maintenance services for both rotary-wing and fixed-wing aircraft. Sikorsky said the Czech company completed a detailed assessment process before being authorised to distribute components, including reviews of its quality, process and policy standards.
ČLS chief executive Monika Kowalczykova said, as quoted in the same news update: “Being appointed an authorized Sikorsky distribution center for the European Union countries marks a significant milestone for ČLS and proves our expertise in modernizations and after-sales support of helicopter platforms.”
The appointment also ties into a wider Black Hawk industrial presence in Central Europe. The S-70 variant is manufactured by PZL Mielec in Poland, another Lockheed Martin company, while regional suppliers already contribute to production and support activities.
Sikorsky said ČLS will also work with the company, PZL Mielec and United Rotorcraft towards the planned introduction of the S-70 FIREHAWK programme in the Czech Republic. Production activity connected with Europe’s first FIREHAWK helicopters began in Poland earlier in 2026, with the aircraft intended for aerial firefighting and emergency response missions.
The FIREHAWK is a modified S-70 designed for civil protection roles, combining the Black Hawk airframe with firefighting equipment and other mission systems. The Czech programme therefore sits alongside the military and security fleet already operating in Europe, broadening the regional sustainment requirement beyond defence users alone.
Sikorsky describes the new Czech facility as part of a regional sustainment strategy that already includes authorised distribution centres in South America, the Middle East and Asia. The ČLS agreement is the first such arrangement inside the European Union.

articles.title: At least 3 dead, 265 others missing in Tibet after landslides hit border area with Nepal, says China
articles.body:
Islamuddin Sajid
26 August 2026•Update: 26 August 2026
China on Wednesday confirmed three dead and 265 missing in the southern Tibet region after landslides hit a border area with Nepal, state media reported.
The latest death toll follows a mudslide along the China-Nepal border in southwest China’s Xizang Autonomous Region, according to Xinhua News.
Officials said the mudslide occurred on the Nepalese side of the border and struck the Gyirong Port border crossing in Gyirong County on Wednesday morning.
Authorities were still verifying the casualties while rescue operations continued, according to the on-site emergency headquarters.
Local authorities have closed all vehicle routes from the town of Gyirong to the border crossing, except those involved in emergency and rescue operations.
The restrictions were imposed after the mudslide damaged roads in the area, making them unsafe for travel.
The disaster also disrupted road links, communications, and power supplies to the Chinese side of the crossing, according to the emergency management bureau of Gyirong County in Xigaze.
The mudslide caused severe casualties and left hundreds of people unaccounted for, according to an initial assessment.
According to Nepalese police, at least 97 persons were killed on the Nepal side and 54 people have been rescued, while the Nepal Tourism Board said separately that it recorded 384 missing people.
Gyirong Port is a major land crossing linking China and Nepal and serves as an important route for trade and movement between the two countries.
An initial assessment provides a possible explanation for the sudden surge that caused widespread destruction along the Lhende and Bhotekoshi rivers.
An analysis of Planet Labs satellite imagery indicates that a snow-and-rock landslide near the border triggered a debris-laden flood in the Lhende River, although authorities continue to assess the disaster and its full effect, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

articles.title: French presidential hopeful Attal sees life at Elysée Palace with romantic partner Séjourné
articles.body:
PARIS — French presidential candidate Gabriel Attal said that if he wins the race to succeed Emmanuel Macron next year, he would move into the Elysée Palace with his romantic partner, EU industry chief Stéphane Séjourné.
“We live together,” he said in an interview on French broadcaster LCI on Tuesday. “But again, we each have our paths, our trajectories. We have no intention of changing that.”
Attal and Séjourné’s relationship poses a potential conflict of interest given the latter’s job as a European commissioner. Séjourné swore an oath upon taking office to prioritize EU interests over national matters, and his term runs beyond the French presidential election in April 2027.
Advertisement
Attal, who leads Macron’s centrist party Renaissance, did not address — nor was he questioned in the interview — that potential conflict.
Spokespersons for the two politicians both declined to comment for this story.
But Attal said in his interview that he and Séjourné, who both rose to prominence while working for Macron, keep their careers separate.
“We have always separated our careers. We are two public figures, but we don’t put ourselves on show together … we each follow our own paths separately,” he said.
The pair were in a civil partnership from 2017 to 2022, while Attal held several ministerial positions — including government spokesperson — and Séjourné was an adviser to Macron before becoming an MEP. They then broke up for two years, before rekindling their relationship in 2024.
Recent polls show Attal trailing both front-runner and leader of the far-right National Rally Marine Le Pen and his main ideological rival, former Prime Minister and centrist contender Edouard Philippe, in the presidential race.

articles.title: Hadi Choopan withdraws from 2026 Mr. Olympia
articles.body:
The 2022 Mr. Olympia champion revealed on Instagram that he had been trying to travel to Dubai to follow up on his U.S. visa, as he has done in previous years. However, he said he was denied entry to the UAE and that his 10-year UAE visa had been canceled, Tehran Times areported.
Choopan cited the current political situation and travel restrictions as major factors behind the decision. He also explained that the stress and uncertainty surrounding his travel and U.S. visa situation would prevent him from preparing for the Olympia at the level required.
As a result, Choopan has decided to withdraw from the 2026 Mr. Olympia.
This will mark Choopan’s first absence from the Mr. Olympia since his debut in 2019, ending a remarkable run of seven consecutive appearances on the sport’s biggest stage.
MNA
